newsitem.title: USA: Premium gasoline may firm on Mobil fire - traders.
newsitem.headline: Premium gasoline may firm on Mobil fire - traders.

text.p: West Coast products traders forecast higher prices for premium grade gasolines following an early morning fire at Mobil Corp's Torrance, Calif., refinery.
"It could put pressure on the premium grades," one trader said.
The fire broke out in a PTR unit, used to upgrade gasoline from low-octane to high-octane. Refinery officials said other units in the system continued to operate.
One trader heard that early morning offers for CARB-grade gasoline jumped three cents to 75 cents a gallon in Los Angeles.
Offers for October cargoes of conventional premium were talked about two cents higher from Thursday at 79 cents.
The spread between regular and premium conventional gasoline in L.A. was seven cents Thursday. The spread for CARB grades stood at four cents.
A spokesman could not immediately say how the fire affected gasoline production.
"No one knows what's happening over there," a trader said.
